name: Tessera Industries Phase Disruptor PD-2 'Glitch'
description: An experimental weapon that generates a localized spatial distortion field at a targeted point, causing matter within the field to briefly phase between states in a way that current physics cannot fully explain. The practical effect is that solid objects within the 1-meter field radius experience a momentary loss of structural integrity — molecular bonds flicker, materials briefly become permeable, and anything caught in the transition snaps back to solidity with catastrophic misalignment. The effect lasts less than a tenth of a second but the material damage is permanent: metal crystallizes along new fault lines, biological tissue suffers cellular disruption, and electronics experience cascading component failure. Tessera's R&D team reportedly does not fully understand why the device works.
specifications:
effect radius: 1 meter at target point
effect duration: 0.08 seconds
effective range: 5-20 meters
power source: Experimental spatial distortion generator
weight: 12 kg with power unit
recharge: 120 seconds between activations
activations per power cell: 3
prototypes: 2 confirmed
story_hooks: A crime scene shows damage consistent with Phase Disruptor exposure — materials aged and crystallized in a perfect sphere — but only two prototypes exist and both are supposedly locked in Tessera's vault.

A Tessera physicist involved in the PD-2 project has disappeared after claiming the device does not distort space — it briefly opens a window to somewhere else, and something on the other side is looking back.

physical_description.visual_profile: A brutalist angular device resembling a handheld spatial projector crossed with a prototype particle accelerator. The silhouette is deliberately asymmetrical — a chunky forward-mounted emission chamber tapering to a reinforced grip assembly. It reads as unfinished, experimental, something that shouldn't exist yet.
physical_description.dimensions: 68 cm length, 22 cm width at widest point (emission chamber), 16 cm grip depth. Barrel-equivalent projection lens: 12 cm diameter.
physical_description.weight_description: Genuinely hefty — 12 kg distributed unevenly toward the front, demanding both hands or a reinforced harness. The imbalance is intentional, forcing the operator's body mass into the stabilization process.
physical_description.primary_material: Reinforced titanium-polymer composite frame with exposed internal spatial distortion coils visible through reinforced viewport panels. Heat-dissipation skeleton of brushed aluminum.
physical_description.finish: Industrial matte gunmetal with oxidized patina in stress areas. Viewport panels show faint iridescent oil-slick discoloration where spatial stress has warped the polycarbonate. Scuff marks and micro-fractures suggest constant recalibration.
physical_description.color_scheme: Slate gray primary with sickly cyan accent lighting around the emission chamber aperture. Exposed copper coils visible through panels glow faint bioluminescent green when charged.
physical_description.grip_texture: Bare titanium with friction-etched grip patterns, slightly warm to touch due to constant power bleed. Wrapped in places with salvaged para-aramid cord for additional purchase.
distinctive_features: Unstabilized chromatic aberration visible around the emission lens even at rest — reality-warping side effect
Four exposed spatial distortion coil sets arranged radially, humming at just-audible frequencies
A small viewport window showing cascading holographic calibration data that never fully stabilizes
Emergency thermal bleed vents along the barrel assembly, permanently charred
Tessera R&D serial plate stamped with cryptic alphanumeric: TS-PD2-PROTO-002-UNSTABLE
Hairline fractures in the polycarbonate viewport, sealed with bio-synthetic putty
A faint smell of ozone and irradiated polymers emanates from active cooling ports
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Tessera Industries logo (angular Φ symbol) etched into the grip plate, deliberately small and off-center. Serial designation: PD-2 'GLITCH' spray-painted in degrading white lettering on the underside. Warning labels long since worn away.
physical_description.condition_typical: Perpetually jury-rigged. Always warm. Calibration lights rarely synchronize. Field units show evidence of emergency field repairs — mismatched heat-sink panels, improvised power conduits with exposed solder. The weapon operates, but barely, as if held together by desperation and theoretical physics.
